title: What is two thirds plus one fifth?
description: Two thirds and one fifth have different fractional units. The lowest common multiple of three and five is fifteen, so both fractions are written in fifteenths and the numerators are added. Keeko doubts the answer by adding the tops and adding the bottoms.
teaching_notes: One idea: use the lowest common multiple of the bottom numbers, rewrite both fractions with it, then add the numerators. Watch for the slip of adding the bottoms.

video_script.why: A learner adds fractions with different fractional units by using the lowest common multiple of the bottom numbers.
video_script.substitution: the book's own sum two thirds plus one fifth
video_script.anchor: two strips of the same length, one cut into three equal parts and one cut into five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the tops and adds the bottoms and gets three eighths. Three eighths is less than one half, but two thirds is already more than one half, so the idea is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: two thirds and one fifth make thirteen fifteenths

final_answer.spoken: two thirds and one fifth make thirteen fifteenths

video_script.fraction_reading: two thirds, one fifth, ten fifteenths, three fifteenths, thirteen fifteenths, three eighths, one half
never_show: three eighths written as the sum before Keeko's doubt
maths_rules: multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15; multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15; the lowest common multiple of 3 and 5 is 15
slip: Keeko adds the tops and the bottoms and gets 3/8; 3/8 < 1/2 < 2/3, so the sum would be smaller than a part
video_script.design: Two strips of the same length, in thirds and in fifths, stay on the board. Both are cut into fifteenths, and the fifteenths are counted.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two strips of the same length, one cut into 3 equal parts with 2 shaded in teal and one cut into 5 equal parts with 1 shaded in amber; the words sum? appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.strips: two strips of the same length appear, cut in thirds and in fifths, with two parts shaded on the first and one part on the second
marks.ask: the words sum? appear between the strips

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is from your book, and it asks for the sum of two thirds and one fifth.
<bookmark mark='strips'/>Thirds and fifths are different fractional units.

beats.on_screen: the two strips hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the multiples of 3 listed: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15; the multiples of 5 listed: 5, 10, 15; 15 appears in both lists and is circled

marks.lists: the multiples of three and of five are listed one under the other
marks.lcm: 15 appears in both lists and is circled with the label lowest common multiple

narration: <bookmark mark='lists'/>The multiples of three are three, six, nine, twelve and fifteen. The multiples of five are five, ten and fifteen.
<bookmark mark='lcm'/>The smallest number in both lists is called the lowest common multiple.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the two fractions are two thirds and one fifth.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum of 2/3 and 1/5
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sum of the two fractions.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the lowest common multiple of 3 and 5 is 15; use 15 as the bottom number

marks.lcm: the lowest common multiple 15 is written
marks.use: the words use 15 as the common bottom number are written

narration: <bookmark mark='lcm'/>Step one, the lowest common multiple of three and five is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='use'/>We write both fractions with fifteen as the bottom number.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, multiply the top and the bottom of two thirds by five. That gives ten fifteenths.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Multiply the top and the bottom of one fifth by three. That gives three fifteenths.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: both in fifteenths; add the numerators: 10 + 3 = 13 fifteenths

marks.add: the shaded fifteenths of both strips slide together and 10 + 3 = 13 fifteenths is written

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, both fractions are in fifteenths, so we add the numerators. Ten plus three is thirteen, and the unit stays one fifteenth.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Thirteen units of one fifteenth make thirteen fifteenths, so two thirds and one fifth make thirteen fifteenths.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two strips
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says add the tops and add the bottoms: 3/8; a strip of 8 equal parts with 3 shaded sits under the halfway mark and the 2/3 strip passes it; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.half: a strip of eight equal parts with three shaded stops before the halfway mark, while the two thirds strip passes it

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks they make three eighths, because two plus one is three and three plus five is eight.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Three eighths is less than one half, but two thirds alone is already more than one half.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A sum cannot be smaller than one of its parts, so we first make the units the same.
